import numpy as np

# Data from Table 2 - Monetary Stocks of Gold and Silver
# FY 1953 to FY 1962 (end of fiscal year)
# Gold ($35 per fine ounce) - independent variable
# Silver ($1.29+ per fine ounce) - dependent variable

years = [1953, 1954, 1955, 1956, 1957, 1958, 1959, 1960, 1961, 1962]
gold = [22462.8, 21927.0, 21677.6, 21799.1, 22622.9, 21356.2, 19704.6, 19322.2, 17550.2, 16435.2]
silver = [3814.3, 3863.1, 3922.4, 3994.5, 4116.6, 4306.0, 4414.1, 4394.5, 4346.5, 4317.4]

# Convert to numpy arrays
x = np.array(gold)
y = np.array(silver)

# Calculate linear regression: silver = a + b * gold
# Using least squares
n = len(x)
sum_x = np.sum(x)
sum_y = np.sum(y)
sum_xy = np.sum(x * y)
sum_x2 = np.sum(x * x)
sum_y2 = np.sum(y * y)

# Calculate slope (b) and intercept (a)
b = (n * sum_xy - sum_x * sum_y) / (n * sum_x2 - sum_x * sum_x)
a = (sum_y - b * sum_x) / n

# Calculate R-squared
y_pred = a + b * x
ss_res = np.sum((y - y_pred) ** 2)
ss_tot = np.sum((y - np.mean(y)) ** 2)
r_squared = 1 - (ss_res / ss_tot)

print("Data points:")
for i in range(n):
    print(f"FY {years[i]}: Gold = {gold[i]}, Silver = {silver[i]}")
print()
print(f"Linear regression: Silver = {a:.4f} + {b:.6f} * Gold")
print(f"R-squared = {r_squared:.6f}")
print(f"R-squared (rounded to 2 decimal places) = {round(r_squared, 2)}")
EOF
